add.issue.comment.md:
Fork (decision: operator, 2026-10-06): the script is not a wrapper around the Aphotic installer. It is shaped like the community-scripts Proxmox VE Helper (community-scripts.org): it runs on the PVE host itself and provides a default and an advanced install function for Proxmox, plus the dev VM lifecycle.

- init: writes a commented ~/.config/aphotic/devvm.env; every host/VM value comes from that file; the example carries no value pointing at anyone's network.
- install: Proxmox VE on a bare Debian host. default = no-subscription repo, PVE kernel, CPU microcode. advanced = --enterprise, --bridge, --ip/--gateway/--dns.
- create-vm: the dev VM from the latest Arch opencloud image. default = the machine that runs a real Hyprland session (q35, OVMF, host CPU, VirtIO-GPU render node, 12 GiB / 6 cores / 60 GiB, cloud-init user + SSH key, DHCP). advanced = one flag per setting (--vmid, --name, --machine, --cpu, --cores, --ram, --disk, --display, --bridge, --storage, --mac, --vlan, --mtu, --user, --ssh-key, --ip, --gateway, --dns, --no-start).
- reset / destroy / status: the dev VM lifecycle, so a failed test is minutes from a clean slate.

Nothing in the script is specific to the Aphotic installer; booting the desktop and running the installer inside the VM are manual steps the docs describe.

tools/devvm/proxmox.sh: a tracked, parameterized Proxmox VE helper, shaped like the community-scripts Proxmox VE Helper (community-scripts.org) — it runs on the PVE host itself.

- init writes a commented ~/.config/aphotic/devvm.env example. Every host/VM value comes from that file; the example carries no value that points at anyone's network.
- install: Proxmox VE on a bare Debian host. default = no-subscription repo, PVE kernel, CPU microcode. advanced = --enterprise, --bridge, --ip/--gateway/--dns.
- create-vm: the dev VM from the latest Arch opencloud image. default = the machine that runs a real Hyprland session (q35, OVMF, host CPU, VirtIO-GPU render node, 12 GiB / 6 cores / 60 GiB, cloud-init user + SSH key, DHCP). advanced = one flag per setting (--vmid, --name, --machine, --cpu, --cores, --ram, --disk, --display, --bridge, --storage, --mac, --vlan, --mtu, --user, --ssh-key, --ip, --gateway, --dns, --no-start).
- reset / destroy / status: the dev VM lifecycle, so a failed test is minutes from a clean slate.

Nothing in the script is specific to the Aphotic installer; booting the desktop and running the installer inside the VM are manual steps the docs describe.

Done when: on a stock Proxmox host, init + create-vm produces a VM that runs a real Hyprland session; install (default and advanced) works on a bare Debian host; shellcheck passes; a test covers argument parsing and config loading without a hypervisor.

add.issue.comment.md:
Found while writing the Dev-VM guide (5NEQQW0): Arch has retired the opencloud images. https://archlinux.org/releng/cloud/ is a 404, the ~arch-releng/images/ mirror directories are gone, and the latest release (2026.10.01) ships only ISOs and the bootstrap tarball. The create-vm path in PR #299 downloaded from that dead page, so it would have failed on any real host.

Fixed in 1b33903 (PR #299 updated): create-vm now follows the community-scripts helper convention it is modelled on. It downloads the latest installer ISO from the official mirror (https://geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com/iso/latest/archlinux-x86_64.iso, overridable with --iso-url / DEVVM_ISO_URL), imports it as the VM's boot disk, grows the disk to the configured size, and boots the live environment. The base system is then installed once in the guest console with archinstall (user, sudo, SSH key, plus openssh and qemu-guest-agent in the package list), which the wiki Dev-VM page documents for both libvirt and Proxmox.

Cloud-init is gone from the VM path with it: the --ip/--gateway/--dns VM options are deleted (they only worked through cloud-init), and status says when the guest agent is not up yet. tools/ci/local.sh is green in the worktree (75 bash files, 238 pytest, shellcheck advisory only). Still not verified on a real PVE host; the ISO URL and the import-as-boot-disk trick are the parts a first real run should confirm.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: the Dev-VM wiki page is live (wiki master, pushed ba8ce7a). It states the guest spec any hypervisor must satisfy (x86_64 KVM, UEFI, VirtIO-GPU, host CPU, 6 cores, 12 GiB, 60 GiB, host-reachable network, user plus SSH key), explains the two settings that decide usability (VirtIO-GPU render node, SPICE not web console), and gives a worked example per path: libvirt/QEMU (virt-install with the installer ISO as boot medium, --cpu host, --ram 12288, --disk size=60, edk2, --video virtio, --graphics spice) for a contributor's own machine, and tools/devvm/proxmox.sh (PR #299, ticket 12QRFSX) for Proxmox. It covers the base-system step honestly: Arch retired the opencloud images, so every path boots the latest installer ISO and installs the base system with archinstall (a --dry-run trick for automation is documented). A short VPS section says what a headless box can and cannot show, and a copy-paste prompt block hands the whole setup to the user's own agent.

Verified: every quoted command, flag, and subcommand on the page passes the 9A2Z2VK docs-drift checker against the repo; the ISO URL and its latest-alias resolve (206); the spec table matches the verified working guest on the Proxmox-Test-VM page.

Could not verify on this machine: the machine runs Aphotic with about 4 GiB of RAM to spare, so a 12 GiB guest cannot start here and virt-install is not installed; the libvirt example was not executed end to end, and the Proxmox path was not run on a real PVE host (that verification belongs with 12QRFSX). A maintainer with a KVM host can confirm the virt-install line verbatim.

add.issue.comment.md: In flight on fix/harness-support (unified branch; adapter PR in aphotic-plugins, consumer half in the core PR). Payload shape verified on this machine with a live `codex exec` one-shot (all six hook events captured): SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd carry session_id, turn_id, transcript_path, cwd, model, permission_mode, tool_name/tool_use_id, reason. The new codex_hook.py builds v2 records directly (no more v1 passthrough), reads the provider off the rollout's session_meta (local providers are not mislabelled openai), and on PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd tails the session log for the newest token_count: per-response last_token_usage becomes a `usage` record (input/output/reasoning/cache tokens) and rate_limits become a `quota` record (primary/secondary usedPercent+resetsAt). A locked per-session sidecar claims each token_count ordinal exactly once, so parallel tool calls and Stop-then-SessionEnd never double-count. Live end-to-end run (real codex + repo adapter + core writer) produced session_start/turn/tool_call/usage/quota/session_end with real token counts and the primary rate-limit window. Core half: AgentProviders folds stream `quota` records into the same map the statusLine file feeds, so the notch tile's quota bars work for Codex, and agent_hook.py maps codex->openai as provider default.
